answer: Each epoch the network issues a saffron‑colored challenge signal to every registered AI, requiring the agent to generate a novel proof of reasoning based on the current tide of public data. The proof must be recomputed from scratch, consuming a fixed amount of model compute that cannot be cached or shared across identities, so a Sybil attacker must pay the full cost for every fake node it creates. Because the compute cost scales linearly with the number of identities, large‑scale impersonation quickly becomes economically prohibitive.
